title: Another Blow For Bonds?
gist: A paywalled teaser notes the 10-year US Treasury yield jumped 18bp to 5.11% (its highest since the 2007 credit crunch) on strong PMI data and rebounding oil prices, and flags a tightening US labor market as a further potential upward force on yields and inflation.

themes.theme: Treasury yields breaking through key levels

insights.claim: The 10-year US Treasury yield jumped 18 basis points in a single session, breaking through 5% to hit 5.11%, its highest level since the credit crunch began in July 2007.
insights.speaker: Tan Kai Xian
insights.so_what: A break above 5% to a post-2007 high on the 10-year is a significant technical and psychological level for rate-sensitive positioning (duration, equities, mortgages), and the move was driven by data surprises rather than a Fed announcement, making it a market-driven rather than policy-driven repricing to track.
insights.quote: the 10-year US treasury yield jumped 18bp Wednesday, breaking through the 5% level to hit 5.11%, its highest since the outbreak of the credit crunch in July 2007
insights.locator: Propelled by much stronger-than-expected PMI readings

insights.claim: The yield jump was driven by much stronger-than-expected PMI readings and a rebound in oil prices, occurring while the Federal Reserve is on a tightening track and inflation pressure remains persistent.
insights.speaker: Tan Kai Xian
insights.so_what: Strong PMI plus rebounding oil simultaneously pushing yields up signals markets are pricing both stronger growth and renewed inflation risk together, a combination that argues against assuming disinflation is now a settled trend.
insights.quote: Propelled by much stronger-than-expected PMI readings and a rebound in the price of oil... few market participants would dismiss the possibility of a further near-term rise in yields.
insights.locator: Propelled by much stronger-than-expected PMI readings

themes.theme: A tightening labor market as a further upside risk to yields

insights.claim: US nonfarm payrolls jumped by a surprisingly strong 162,000 in August, though the three-month moving average of payroll growth stood at 71,000, comfortably within the estimated breakeven range of 15,000-87,000 needed to keep the unemployment rate stable.
insights.speaker: Tan Kai Xian
insights.so_what: The gap between the strong single-month print (162,000) and the calmer three-month trend (71,000) means the labor market is not yet clearly overheating on trend data alone, so a single strong payrolls report shouldn't be read in isolation as confirming a tightening cycle.
insights.quote: payrolls jumped by a surprisingly strong 162,000 in August... The three-month moving average of payrolls growth is at 71,000, comfortably within its currently estimated breakeven range of 15,000-87,000
insights.locator: The US labor market has been largely quiescent

insights.claim: The author flags growing signs the US labor market may be set to tighten, which would push both wage growth and inflation higher, as a further force that could add upward pressure on Treasury yields beyond the PMI and oil-driven move.
insights.speaker: Tan Kai Xian
insights.so_what: If the labor market tightening thesis plays out, it would compound the already-rising-yield narrative, reinforcing a case for continued bond-market caution rather than expecting a near-term yield peak.
insights.quote: there is another force that may emerge to exert upward pressure on yields: there are growing signs that the US labor market may be set to tighten, pushing both wage growth and inflation higher
insights.locator: In addition, there is another force
